scope: Fresh read-only sequence analyses and primary-record queries, performed with HemK's published RF-methyltransferase function already known. These are not blind discovery, historical reproductions or proposed library categories.

queries_in_actual_call_order: organism_id:83333 AND (gene:prmC OR gene:prmB OR gene:dam OR gene:hemG)
accession:P0ACC1 OR accession:P39199 OR accession:P0AEE8 OR accession:P0ACB4
input_acquisition.limitations: The M.TaqI name query returned other records as well; only reviewed P14385 from Thermus aquaticus was selected. Modern annotation names were visible, so this is explicitly informed analysis. Current labels were not treated as independent proof of function.

routes.goal_and_start: Assess how much of a DNA-methyltransferase interpretation is supported by HemK's sequence. Start with the historical NPPY argument and actual E. coli HemK sequence, not its present function label.

steps.selected_question: Does the familiar E. coli DNA adenine methylase Dam share a motif and a broader corresponding region?
steps.actual_probe: Fetch P0ACC1 and P0AEE8 sequences, search the [SND]PP[YFW] pattern, then compute optimal local BLOSUM62 alignment with gap open -11 and extension -1.
steps.actual_result: HemK has NPPY at residue 183; Dam has DPPY at residue 181. The best local alignment instead covered only 19 residue pairs, with 7 identities and raw score 38, and did not pair those two motifs.
steps.changed_interpretation: Matching small motifs and similar residue positions did not provide a convincing broad comparison. Dam was an insufficient representative for the particular gamma-class comparison in the papers. A short optimal alignment is not evidence that the proteins lack evolutionary relationship.
steps.next_selected_probe: Use the gamma-family DNA enzyme M.TaqI, directly compared with HemK in the 2004 primary structural paper.

steps.selected_question: Does a more relevant DNA reference yield a coherent comparison, and what would that comparison actually establish?
steps.actual_probe: Retrieve reviewed Thermus aquaticus P14385 from the M.TaqI name-query results and apply exactly the same local alignment settings.
steps.actual_result: M.TaqI contains NPPY at residue 105. Its optimal alignment to HemK had 104 aligned residue pairs, 30 identities, 13 gap characters and raw score 47; the shared NPPY aligned at the end of the region.
steps.changed_interpretation: This gives a broader candidate catalytic-region comparison than Dam, but is weak, uncalibrated sequence evidence. It does not discriminate DNA from protein substrate.
steps.next_selected_probe: Inspect the primary paper's explicit active-site comparison rather than interpreting the motif as substrate evidence.

steps.selected_question: Can the catalytic motif comparison distinguish the target substrate class?
steps.actual_probe: Primary query: HemK M.TaqI NPPY active-site comparison; inspect Yang et al. 2004 results.
steps.actual_result: The paper reports superposable NPPY active-site geometry across HemK and DNA amino-methyltransferase M.TaqI, supporting conserved amino-group chemistry despite different substrates.
steps.changed_interpretation: The discriminating question is substrate recognition, not whether the short motif exists.
steps.bounded_conclusion: The route supplies catalytic-family compatibility and a reason to withhold a DNA-specific annotation. It does not establish release-factor specificity from sequence alone.

routes.goal_and_start: Ask which E. coli protein is most related in sequence to experimentally characterized L3 glutamine methyltransferase PrmB/YfcB, without presuming that its L3 substrate should transfer.

steps.selected_question: Among this retrieved K-12 proteome, is there a nonself protein standing out as a PrmB-related candidate?
steps.actual_probe: Retrieve all FASTA records returned for proteome UP000000625 and score P39199 against every nonself sequence using the same local BLOSUM62 settings.
steps.actual_result: There were 4403 FASTA records. HemK P0ACC1 ranked first nonself with raw score 254; next was TrmN6 P31825 at 103, then RsmC P39406 at 92. Three selenoproteins contained U outside BLOSUM62 and were scored after masking U to X; their identities are recorded in the score artifact.
steps.changed_interpretation: HemK was the outstanding candidate within this one reference/proteome comparison, giving a concrete reason to examine its alignment. These are raw scores, not significance estimates or evidence that no other homolog exists.
steps.next_selected_probe: Inspect whether the relationship extends beyond the short NPPY motif.

steps.selected_question: Is the PrmB relationship only a motif coincidence or a wider aligned core?
steps.actual_probe: Compute and inspect the full optimal HemK-P39199 local alignment.
steps.actual_result: The alignment spans HemK residues 48-239 and PrmB residues 70-263, with 192 aligned residue pairs, 63 identities, two gap characters and raw score 254. Both NPPY motifs align within a wider shared region.
steps.changed_interpretation: The sequence relationship supports pursuing related catalytic chemistry; terminal differences remain outside much of the matched core.
steps.next_selected_probe: Query the primary substrate evidence to test whether homology justifies copying the reference's L3 specificity.

steps.selected_question: Does the characterized reference's substrate specificity transfer to HemK?
steps.actual_probe: Inspect the 2002 EMBO YfcB and HemK substrate experiments and the independent PNAS HemK results.
steps.actual_result: YfcB methylated L3 but not RF1/RF2, while HemK preparations methylated release factors; hemK disruption removed RF1 methylation. GGQ replacements prevented the observed HemK-dependent modification in the EMBO tests.
steps.changed_interpretation: Shared chemistry survived comparison, while identical substrate specificity did not.
steps.bounded_conclusion: The fresh sequence analysis prioritizes a protein-glutamine-methyltransferase relationship. The exact release-factor assignment is accepted from published experiments, not claimed as a new result of this score search.

failures_and_missing_data: System python lacked Biopython, so the existing repository virtual-environment Python with Biopython was used; no dependency was installed.
The first proteome score attempt failed on selenocysteine U. The completed analysis explicitly masks nonmatrix symbols to X and records affected proteins.
The NCBI BLAST skill requires a contact email; NCBI_EMAIL was absent. No address was fabricated, no NCBI job was submitted, and there is no RID or BLAST E-value.
No wet-lab validation, phylogeny, new annotation run or functional database update occurred.
actual_capabilities_used: UniProt REST search/stream via the installed uniprot-skill script: accession/name/proteome query in; current sequence records and FASTA out.
Existing Biopython PairwiseAligner: actual amino-acid sequences plus declared scoring parameters in; coordinates, raw optimal local score and alignment out.
Web queries of primary papers: targeted biological question in; reported method/result sections out.
